OFFERING CIRCULAR DATED 7 SEPTEMBER 2026




           "THE ETHNIKI" HELLENIC GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY S.A.

        (a société anonyme incorporated and existing under the laws of the Hellenic Republic)
€100,000,000 6.875 per cent. Reset Subordinated Restricted Tier 1 Perpetual Temporary Write-
                                         Down Notes
                                    Issue Price: 100.000 per cent.
The €100,000,000 6.875 per cent. Reset Subordinated Restricted Tier 1 Perpetual Temporary Write-
Down Notes (the "Notes") are issued by "The Ethniki" Hellenic General Insurance Company S.A. (the
"Issuer" or "Ethniki").
References herein to the "Conditions" shall be construed as references to the Terms and Conditions of
the Notes and references to a numbered "Condition" shall be construed accordingly.
The Notes bear interest on their Prevailing Principal Amount (as defined in the Conditions) (i) from
(and including) the Issue Date to (but excluding) 9 March 2032 (the "First Reset Date") at the rate of
6.875 per cent. per annum and (ii) in respect of each Reset Period (as defined in the Conditions)
thereafter at the applicable Reset Rate of Interest (as defined in the Conditions), which will be
determined by the Agent (as defined in the Conditions) on the relevant Reset Determination Date (as
defined in the Conditions) as the sum of the relevant Reset Reference Rate (as defined in the Conditions)
and the Margin (as defined in the Conditions), payable in each case (subject to the following proviso)
semi-annually in arrear on 9 March and 9 September in each year commencing on 9 March 2027;
provided that the Issuer may at its discretion at any time elect to cancel any payment of interest on the
Notes, in whole or in part, and must cancel a payment of interest (i) in the circumstances described in
Conditions 5(b) and 5(c) and (ii) if and to the extent that such payment could not be made in compliance
with the Solvency Condition (as defined in the Conditions). Any interest payment (or, as the case may
be, part thereof) which is so cancelled will not accumulate or be payable at any time thereafter, no
amount will become due from the Issuer in respect thereof and cancellation thereof shall not constitute
a default for any purpose on the part of the Issuer. Payments on the Notes will be made without
deduction for or on account of taxes of any Taxing Jurisdiction (as defined in the Conditions) to the
extent described in Condition 9.
Upon the occurrence of a Trigger Event, the Prevailing Principal Amount of each Note will be
immediately and mandatorily Written Down by the relevant Write Down Amount and any interest
accrued to the relevant Write Down Date (each term as defined in the Conditions) and unpaid shall be
cancelled in accordance with the Conditions. Noteholders may lose some or all of their investment as a
result of such a Write Down. Following such a Write Down, the Issuer may, in certain circumstances
and at its sole and full discretion, Write Up (as defined in the Conditions) the Prevailing Principal
Amount of each Note, in accordance with the Conditions.
The Notes are perpetual securities with no fixed redemption date. Subject to the Issuer having complied
with any applicable Regulatory Conditions (as defined in the Conditions), to no Regulatory Deficiency
Redemption Deferral Event (as defined in the Conditions) having occurred and continuing and to the
requirements set out in Condition 7(b), the Issuer will have the right to redeem all the Notes (but not
some only) (i) (A) in the period from (and including) 9 September 2031 to (and including) the First
Reset Date or (B) on any Interest Payment Date thereafter, (ii) upon the occurrence of a Deductibility
Event (as defined in the Conditions), a Gross-up Event (as defined in the Conditions) or a Capital



                                                   -i-

Disqualification Event (as defined in the Conditions) or (iii) if 75 per cent. or more of the aggregate
principal amount (determined, solely for these purposes, as though all outstanding Notes remain at their
Initial Principal Amount (as defined in the Conditions)) of the Notes originally issued (and, for these
purposes, any Further Notes (as defined in the Conditions) issued pursuant to Condition 17 will be
deemed to have been originally issued) have been purchased by the Issuer or any of its Subsidiaries
and, in each case, cancelled pursuant to the Conditions (as further described in Condition 7(f)), in each
case at their Prevailing Principal Amount, together with (to the extent not previously cancelled in
accordance with the Conditions) any unpaid interest accrued to (but excluding) the date fixed for
redemption. The Issuer will, upon the occurrence of a Deductibility Event, a Gross-up Event or a Capital
Disqualification Event, or in order to ensure the effectiveness and enforceability of Condition 20(d),
also have the right to substitute the Notes for, or vary the terms of the Notes so that they remain or
become (as applicable) Qualifying Tier 1 Notes (as defined in the Conditions), all as described in
Condition 7.
The Notes are direct, unsecured and subordinated obligations of the Issuer, ranking pari passu and
without preference amongst themselves. See Condition 3.
Application has been made to the Luxembourg Stock Exchange for the Notes to be admitted to trading
on the Euro MTF market of the Luxembourg Stock Exchange and to be listed on the Official List of the
Luxembourg Stock Exchange. This Offering Circular constitutes a prospectus for the purpose of Part
IV of the Luxembourg law on prospectuses for securities dated 16 July 2019. References in this Offering
Circular to the Notes being "listed" (and all related references) shall mean that the Notes have been
admitted to trading on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange's Euro MTF market and have been admitted to
the Official List of the Luxembourg Stock Exchange. The Luxembourg Stock Exchange's Euro MTF
market is neither a regulated market for the purposes of Directive 2014/65/EU (as amended, "MiFID
II") nor a UK regulated market for the purposes of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 on markets in
financial instruments as it forms part of United Kingdom ("UK") domestic law by virtue of the
European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018 ("UK MiFIR").
The Notes will initially be represented by a global certificate in registered form (the "Global
Certificate") which will be registered on 9 September 2026 (the "Issue Date") in the name of a nominee
of a common depositary for Euroclear Bank SA/NV ("Euroclear") and Clearstream Banking S.A.
("Clearstream, Luxembourg"). Interests in the Global Certificate will be exchangeable for definitive
Notes ("Certificates") only in certain limited circumstances, all as further described in "Form of the
Notes and Summary of Provisions Relating to the Notes While in Global Form" below.
An investment in the Notes involves risks. For a discussion of certain of these risks see "Risk
Factors".
The Notes have not received a rating from any credit rating agency as at the date of this Offering
Circular.


                                       Sole Global Coordinator

                                  Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE

                                         Joint Lead Managers

 Goldman Sachs Bank Europe                   Piraeus Bank                  UBS Investment Bank
            SE

The date of this Offering Circular is 7 September 2026.




                                                  - ii -

IMPORTANT INFORMATION

The Issuer accepts responsibility for the information contained in this Offering Circular. To the best of
the knowledge and belief of the Issuer (having taken all reasonable care to ensure that such is the case)
the information contained in this Offering Circular is in accordance with the facts and does not omit
anything which in the context of the issuance and offering of the Notes would be misleading and affect
the import of such information.

This Offering Circular is to be read in conjunction with all documents which are deemed to be
incorporated herein by reference (see "Documents Incorporated by Reference" below). This Offering
Circular shall be read and construed on the basis that such documents are incorporated into and form
part of this Offering Circular.

Other than in relation to the documents which are deemed to be incorporated by reference (see
"Documents Incorporated by Reference" below), the information on the websites to which this Offering
Circular refers does not form part of this Offering Circular.

None of the Joint Lead Managers (as defined in "Subscription and Sale" below) has independently
verified the information contained herein. Accordingly, no representation, warranty or undertaking,
express or implied, is made and no responsibility or liability is accepted by any of the Joint Lead
Managers as to the accuracy or completeness of the information contained in this Offering Circular or
any other information provided by the Issuer in connection with the Notes or their distribution.

Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE, UBS Europe SE (the "Relevant Joint Lead Managers") and their
respective affiliates have engaged, and may in the future engage, in investment banking and/or
commercial banking transactions with, and may provide services to, the Issuer and its affiliates in the
ordinary course of business. In addition, in the ordinary course of their business activities, the Relevant
Joint Lead Managers and their respective affiliates may make or hold a broad array of investments and
actively trade debt and equity securities (or related derivative securities) and financial instruments
(including bank loans) for their own account and for the accounts of their customers. Such investments
and securities activities may involve securities and/or instruments of the Issuer or the Issuer's affiliates.
The Relevant Joint Lead Managers and their respective affiliates may have a lending relationship with
the Issuer and may routinely hedge their credit exposure to the Issuer consistent with their customary
risk management policies. Typically, the Relevant Joint Lead Managers and their respective affiliates
would hedge such exposure by entering into transactions which consist of either the purchase of credit
default swaps or the creation of short positions in securities, including potentially the Notes. Any such
short positions could adversely affect future trading prices of the Notes. The Relevant Joint Lead
Managers and their respective affiliates may also make investment recommendations and/or publish or
express independent research views in respect of such securities or financial instruments and may hold,
or recommend to clients that they acquire, long and/or short positions in such securities and instruments.
For the avoidance of doubt, the term "affiliates" also includes parent companies. Piraeus Bank S.A. is
the ultimate parent company of the Issuer.

No person is or has been authorised by the Issuer to give any information or to make any representation
not contained in or not consistent with this Offering Circular or any other information provided in
connection with the Notes and, if given or made, such information or representation must not be relied
upon as having been authorised by the Issuer or the Joint Lead Managers.

Neither this Offering Circular nor any other information supplied in connection with the Notes (i) is
intended to provide the basis of any credit or other evaluation or (ii) should be considered as a
recommendation or as constituting an invitation or offer by the Issuer or the Joint Lead Managers that
any recipient of this Offering Circular or any other information supplied in connection with the Notes
should purchase the Notes. Each investor contemplating purchasing the Notes should make its own
independent investigation of the financial condition and affairs, and its own appraisal of the



                                                    - iii -

creditworthiness, of the Issuer. Neither this Offering Circular nor any other information supplied in
connection with the Notes constitutes an offer or invitation by or on behalf of the Issuer or the Joint
Lead Managers to any person to subscribe for or to purchase the Notes.

Neither the delivery of this Offering Circular nor the offering, sale or delivery of the Notes shall in any
circumstances imply that the information contained in this Offering Circular concerning the Issuer is
correct at any time subsequent to its date or that any other information supplied in connection with the
Notes is correct as of any time subsequent to the date indicated in the document containing the same.
The Joint Lead Managers expressly do not undertake to review the financial condition or affairs of the
Issuer or to advise any investor in the Notes of any information coming to their attention.

RESTRICTIONS ON MARKETING AND SALES TO RETAIL INVESTORS – The Notes are
complex financial instruments with high risk and are not a suitable or appropriate investment for all
investors, especially retail investors. In some jurisdictions, regulatory authorities have adopted or
published laws, regulations or guidance with respect to the offer or sale of certain securities with
characteristics similar to the Notes. Potential investors in the Notes should inform themselves of, and
comply with, any applicable laws, regulations or regulatory guidance with respect to any resale of the
Notes (or any beneficial interests therein).

In the UK, the FCA Conduct of Business Sourcebook ("COBS") requires, in summary, that certain
securities with characteristics similar to the Notes should not be offered or sold to retail clients (as
defined in COBS 3.4 and each a "retail client") in the UK.

Potential investors should inform themselves of, and comply with, any applicable laws, regulations or
regulatory guidance with respect to any resale of the Notes (or any beneficial interests therein),
including COBS.

Some or all of the Issuer and the Joint Lead Managers are required to comply with some or all of COBS.
By purchasing, or making or accepting an offer to purchase, any Notes (or any beneficial interests
therein) from the Issuer and/or the Joint Lead Managers, each prospective investor represents, warrants,
agrees with and undertakes to the Issuer and the Joint Lead Managers that:

(a)     it is not a retail client in the UK; and

(b)     whether or not it is subject to COBS, it will not:

        (i)      sell or offer the Notes (or any beneficial interests therein) to retail clients in the UK; or

        (ii)     communicate (including the distribution of this Offering Circular) or approve an
                 invitation or inducement to participate in, acquire or underwrite the Notes (or any
                 beneficial interests therein) where that communication, invitation or inducement is
                 addressed to or disseminated in such a way that it is likely to be received by a retail
                 client in the UK,

        and in selling or offering the Notes or making or approving communications relating to the
        Notes, it may not rely on the limited exemptions set out in COBS.

The obligations above are in addition to the need to comply at all times with all applicable laws,
regulations and regulatory guidance (whether inside or outside the European Economic Area (the
"EEA") or the UK) relating to the promotion, offering, distribution and/or sale of the Notes (or any
beneficial interests therein), whether or not specifically mentioned in this Offering Circular, including
(without limitation) any requirements under MiFID II, the UK FCA Handbook and any other applicable
laws, regulations and regulatory guidance relating to determining the appropriateness and/or suitability




                                                    - iv -

of an investment in the Notes (or any beneficial interests therein) by investors in any relevant
jurisdiction.

Where acting as agent on behalf of a disclosed or undisclosed client when purchasing, or making or
accepting an offer to purchase, the Notes (or any beneficial interests therein) from the Issuer and/or the
Joint Lead Managers, the foregoing representations, warranties, agreements and undertakings will be
given by and be binding upon both the agent and its underlying client.

IMPORTANT – EEA RETAIL INVESTORS – The Notes are not intended to be offered, sold or
otherwise made available to and should not be offered, sold or otherwise made available to, any retail
investor in the EEA. For these purposes, a retail investor means a person who is one (or both) of (i) a
retail client as defined in point (11) of Article 4(1) of MiFID II; or (ii) a customer within the meaning
of Directive (EU) 2016/97 (as amended, the "Insurance Distribution Directive"), where that customer
would not qualify as a professional client as defined in point (10) of Article 4(1) of MiFID II.
Consequently no key information document required by Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014 (as amended,
the "PRIIPs Regulation") for offering or selling the Notes or otherwise making them available to retail
investors in the EEA has been prepared and therefore offering or selling the Notes or otherwise making
them available to any retail investor in the EEA may be unlawful under the PRIIPs Regulation.

IMPORTANT – UK RETAIL INVESTORS – The Notes are not intended to be offered, sold,
distributed or otherwise made available to and should not be offered, sold, distributed or otherwise made
available to any retail investor in the UK. For these purposes, a retail investor means a person who is
not a professional client, as defined in point (8) of Article 2(1) of UK MiFIR. Consequently no
disclosure document required by the FCA Product Disclosure Sourcebook ("DISC") for offering,
selling or distributing the Notes or otherwise making them available to retail investors in the UK has
been prepared and therefore offering, selling or distributing the Notes or otherwise making them
available to any retail investor in the UK may be unlawful under DISC and the Consumer Composite
Investments (Designated Activities) Regulations 2024, as applicable.

MiFID II product governance / Professional investors and ECPs only target market – Solely for
the purposes of each manufacturer's product approval process, the target market assessment in respect
of the Notes has led to the conclusion that: (i) the target market for the Notes is eligible counterparties
and professional clients only, each as defined in MiFID II; and (ii) all channels for distribution of the
Notes to eligible counterparties and professional clients are appropriate. Any person subsequently
offering, selling or recommending the Notes (a "distributor") should take into consideration the
manufacturers' target market assessment; however, a distributor subject to MiFID II is responsible for
undertaking its own target market assessment in respect of the Notes (by either adopting or refining the
manufacturers' target market assessment) and determining appropriate distribution channels.

UK MiFIR product governance / Professional investors and ECPs only target market – Solely for
the purposes of the manufacturer's product approval process, the target market assessment in respect of
the Notes has led to the conclusion that: (i) the target market for the Notes is only eligible counterparties,
as defined in the FCA Handbook Conduct of Business Sourcebook, and professional clients, as defined
in UK MiFIR; and (ii) all channels for distribution of the Notes to eligible counterparties and
professional clients are appropriate. Any distributor should take into consideration the manufacturer's
target market assessment; however, a distributor subject to the FCA Handbook Product Intervention
and Product Governance Sourcebook is responsible for undertaking its own target market assessment
in respect of the Notes (by either adopting or refining the manufacturer's target market assessment) and
determining appropriate distribution channels.




                                                     -v-

SALES TO CANADA

The Notes may be sold only to purchasers purchasing, or deemed to be purchasing, as principal that are
accredited investors, as defined in National Instrument 45-106 Prospectus Exemptions or subsection
73.3(1) of the Securities Act (Ontario), and are permitted clients, as defined in National Instrument 31-
103 Registration Requirements, Exemptions and Ongoing Registrant Obligations. Any resale of the
Notes must be made in accordance with an exemption from, or in a transaction not subject to, the
prospectus requirements of applicable securities laws.

Securities legislation in certain provinces or territories of Canada may provide a purchaser with
remedies for rescission or damages if this Offering Circular (including any amendment thereto) contains
a misrepresentation, provided that the remedies for rescission or damages are exercised by the purchaser
within the time limit prescribed by the securities legislation of the purchaser's province or territory. The
purchaser should refer to any applicable provisions of the securities legislation of the purchaser's
province or territory for particulars of these rights or consult with a legal advisor.




                                                    - vi -

THE NOTES ARE COMPLEX FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS

The Notes are high risk and complex financial instruments and such instruments may be purchased by
investors as a way to reduce risk or enhance yield with an understood, measured, appropriate addition
of risk to their overall portfolios. Each potential investor in the Notes must determine the suitability of
that investment in light of its own circumstances. In particular, each potential investor may wish to
consider, either on its own or with the help of its financial and other professional advisers, whether it:

•       has sufficient knowledge and experience to make a meaningful evaluation of the Notes, the
        merits and risks of investing in the Notes and the information contained or incorporated by
        reference in this Offering Circular or any applicable supplement;

•       has access to, and knowledge of, appropriate analytical tools to evaluate, in the context of its
        particular financial situation, an investment in the Notes and the impact the Notes will have on
        its overall investment portfolio;

•       has sufficient financial resources and liquidity to bear all of the risks of an investment in the
        Notes, including where the currency for principal or interest payments (being euro) is different
        from the potential investor's currency and the possibility that the entire principal amount of the
        Notes could be lost, including as a result of a Write Down of the Prevailing Principal Amount
        or following the exercise of any statutory loss absorption power by the Relevant Resolution
        Authority (as defined in the Conditions);

•       understands thoroughly the terms of the Notes, such as their perpetual nature, the possibility of
        the Prevailing Principal Amount being subject to a Write Down, the provisions governing
        cancellation of interest payments on the Notes or deferral of redemption of the Notes, and is
        familiar with the behaviour of any relevant indices and financial markets; and

•       is able to evaluate (either alone or with the help of financial, legal or tax advisors) possible
        scenarios for economic, interest rate and other factors that may affect its investment and its
        ability to bear the applicable risks.

Legal investment considerations may restrict certain investments. The investment activities of certain
investors are subject to legal investment laws and regulations, or review or regulation by certain
authorities. Each potential investor should consult its legal advisers to determine whether and to what
extent (1) the Notes are legal investments for it, (2) the Notes can be used as collateral for various types
of borrowing and (3) other restrictions apply to its purchase or pledge of the Notes. Financial institutions
should consult their legal advisers or the appropriate regulators to determine the appropriate treatment
of the Notes under any applicable risk-based capital or similar rules.

The Notes may have no established trading market when issued, and one may never develop.




                                                   - vii -

STABILISATION

In connection with the issue of the Notes, Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE (the "Stabilisation
Manager") (or persons acting on behalf of the Stabilisation Manager) may over-allot Notes or
effect transactions with a view to supporting the market price of the Notes at a level higher than
that which might otherwise prevail. However, stabilisation may not necessarily occur. Any
stabilisation action may begin on or after the date on which adequate public disclosure of the
terms of the offer of the Notes is made and, if begun, may cease at any time, but it must end no
later than the earlier of 30 days after the Issue Date and 60 days after the date of the allotment of
the Notes. Any stabilisation action or over-allotment must be conducted by the Stabilisation
Manager (or persons acting on behalf of the Stabilisation Manager) in accordance with all
applicable laws and rules.




                                                - viii -

IMPORTANT INFORMATION RELATING TO THE USE OF THIS OFFERING CIRCULAR AND
                       THE OFFER OF THE NOTES

This Offering Circular does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy the
Notes in any jurisdiction to any person to whom it is unlawful to make the offer or solicitation in
such jurisdiction. The distribution of this Offering Circular and the offer or sale of the Notes may
be restricted by law in certain jurisdictions. Neither the Issuer nor any of the Joint Lead
Managers represents that this Offering Circular may be lawfully distributed, or that the Notes
may be lawfully offered, in compliance with any applicable registration or other requirements in
any such jurisdiction, or pursuant to an exemption available thereunder, or assumes any
responsibility for facilitating any such distribution or offering. In particular, no action has been
taken by the Issuer or the Joint Lead Managers which is intended to permit a public offering of
the Notes or distribution of this Offering Circular in any jurisdiction. Accordingly, the Notes may
not be offered or sold, directly or indirectly, and neither this Offering Circular nor any
advertisement or other offering material may be distributed or published, in any jurisdiction
except under circumstances that will result in compliance with any applicable laws and
regulations. Persons into whose possession this Offering Circular or the Notes may come must
inform themselves about, and observe, any such restrictions on the distribution of this Offering
Circular and the offering and sale of the Notes. For details of certain restrictions on the
distribution of this Offering Circular and the offer or sale of the Notes in the United States, the
UK and the EEA (including Greece), see "Subscription and Sale" below.

The Notes have not been and will not be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as
amended (the "Securities Act") and may not be offered, sold or delivered within the United States or
to, or for the account or benefit of, U.S. persons (see "Subscription and Sale").

This Offering Circular shall only be used for the purposes for which it has been published.




                                                 - ix -

FORWARD-LOOKING STATEMENTS

This Offering Circular includes forward-looking statements. These include statements relating to,
among other things, the future financial performance of the Issuer and the Group (as defined below),
plans, objectives, goals, strategies and expectations regarding developments in the business, growth and
profitability of the Group and general industry and business conditions applicable to the Group and the
assumptions underlying these forward-looking statements. The Issuer has based these forward-looking
statements on its current expectations, assumptions, estimates and projections about future events.
Although the Issuer believes that the expectations, assumptions, estimates and projections reflected in
its forward-looking statements are reasonable at the date of this Offering Circular, these forward-
looking statements are subject to a number of risks, uncertainties and assumptions that may cause the
actual results, performance or achievements of the Group or those of its industry to be materially
different from or worse than these forward-looking statements. Any forward-looking statements
contained in this Offering Circular speak only as at the date of this Offering Circular. The Issuer does
not assume any obligation to update such forward-looking statements and to adapt them to future events
or developments except to the extent required by law.

The Issuer does not undertake any obligation to publicly update or revise any forward-looking
statements, whether as a result of new information, future events or otherwise. In light of these risks,
uncertainties and assumptions, the forward-looking events discussed in this Offering Circular might not
occur. Any statements regarding past trends or activities should not be taken as a representation that
such trends or activities will continue in the future. Investors are cautioned not to place undue reliance
on such forward-looking statements, which are based on facts known to the Issuer only as at the date of
this Offering Circular. The Issuer has not made any profit forecasts for the current financial year or for
the future. It may, however, inform the investment community from time to time of its financial
performance or any other material event through regular or ad hoc press releases.




                                                   -x-

DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

In this Offering Circular, references to the "Group" are to Ethniki Holdings S.à r.l. and its subsidiaries;
references to "Greece" are to the country, the official name of which is the Hellenic Republic; and
references to "€" and "euro" are to the single currency introduced at the start of the third stage of
European economic and monetary union pursuant to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European
Union, as amended.

The language of this Offering Circular is English.

References to websites or uniform resource locators ("URLs") are inactive textual references and are
included for information purposes only. Unless otherwise specified herein, the contents of any such
website or URL shall not form part of, and shall not be deemed to be incorporated into, this Offering
Circular.

In this Offering Circular, unless the contrary intention appears, a reference to a law or provision of a
law is a reference to that law or provision as extended, amended or re-enacted.




                                                   - xi -

PRESENTATION OF FINANCIAL AND OTHER INFORMATION

The 2024 Annual Financial Report, the 2025 Annual Financial Report and the 2026 Six-month
Financial Report (each as defined herein) were prepared in accordance with International Financial
Reporting Standards ("IFRS") as adopted by the EU and the financial statements included therein were:

        (i)      in respect of the financial statements included in the 2024 Annual Financial Report:
                 audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers S.A., the Issuer's statutory auditors in respect of
                 the year ended 31 December 2024;

        (ii)     in respect of the financial statements included in the 2025 Annual Financial Report:
                 audited by Deloitte Certified Public Accountants S.A., the Issuer's statutory auditors in
                 respect of the year ended 31 December 2025; and

        (iii)    in respect of the financial statements included in the 2026 Six-month Financial Report:
                 reviewed by Deloitte Certified Public Accountants S.A., the Issuer's current statutory
                 auditors.

The 2024 Annual Financial Report presents both consolidated and unconsolidated financial information
of the Issuer, while the 2025 Annual Financial Report and the 2026 Six-month Financial Report present
only unconsolidated financial information of the Issuer and, accordingly, the comparative financial
information in the 2025 Annual Financial Report and the 2026 Six-month Financial Report relates to
unconsolidated financial information only.

During 2025, a number of significant transactions occurred which altered the structure of the Group. In
particular, the Issuer completed the sale of its former subsidiaries, Ethniki Insurance (Cyprus) Limited
and Garanta Asigurari S.A. The impact of these disposals on the Issuer's separate financial statements
is described, as applicable, in notes 10, 13, 16 and 23 to the financial statements of the Issuer for the
year ended 31 December 2025, as included in the 2025 Annual Financial Report.

In September 2025, the Issuer entered into an agreement with the Syngelidis Group for the acquisition
of a 55 per cent. majority interest in ELYZE ANONYMI ETAIREIA ASFALISTIKON PRAKTORON
KAI SYNTONISTON ASFALISTIKON PRAKTORON S.A. ("Elysee Insurance Agent &
Coordinator S.A.") and ELYZE MESITES ASFALISEON S.A. ("Elysee Insurance Brokers S.A.").
On 26 November 2025, Piraeus Financial Holdings S.A. (absorbed by Piraeus Bank S.A. ("Piraeus")
in December 2025) completed the acquisition from CVC Capital Partners Fund VII and National Bank
of Greece of 100 per cent. of the shares of the Issuer's parent company, Ethniki Holdings S.à r.l.
("Ethniki Holdings"). In accordance with IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements, a parent that is
itself a subsidiary (for example, the Issuer, being a parent company as well as a subsidiary of Piraeus)
is not required to prepare consolidated financial statements and, accordingly, the Issuer was not required
to prepare consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025.

It should be noted that the subsidiaries that remain under the control of the Issuer at the date of this
Offering Circular (but which are not fully included in the unconsolidated accounts of the Issuer) had
total assets of €3.6 million (2024: nil), net assets of €2.6 million (2024: nil) and revenue of €0.3 million
(2024: nil) as at and for the year ended 31 December 2025. As at and for the six-month period ended
30 June 2026, such subsidiaries had total assets of €4.1 million, net assets of €3.0 million and revenue
of €1.2 million. Such subsidiaries appear in the unconsolidated financial statements of the Issuer as
investments held at cost less any impairment loss; see further notes 2.4 (Exemption from Presenting
Consolidated Financial Statements) and 16 (Investment In Subsidiaries) to the financial statements of
the Issuer for the year ended 31 December 2025, as included in the 2025 Annual Financial Report.




                                                   - xii -

Certain financial and other information presented in this Offering Circular has been prepared on the
basis of the Issuer's own internal accounts, statistics and estimates, and has not been subject to any audit
or review by the Issuer's statutory auditors.

The Issuer's financial year ends on 31 December of each year. References to any financial year refer to
the year ended 31 December of the calendar year specified.

Certain monetary amounts and other figures included in this Offering Circular have been subject to
rounding adjustments. Accordingly, any discrepancies in any tables between the totals and the sums of
the amounts listed are due to rounding.




                                                   - xiii -

RISK FACTORS

The Issuer believes that the following factors may affect its ability to fulfil its obligations under the
Notes. Most of these factors are contingencies which may or may not occur and the Issuer is not in a
position to express a view on the likelihood of any such contingency occurring.

In addition, factors which are material for the purpose of assessing the market risks associated with the
Notes are also described below.

in the Notes but the inability of the Issuer to pay interest, principal or other amounts on or in connection

Financial and economic risks

The level of, and volatility in, interest rates may adversely affect the Issuer's businesses.

To be able to meet their future liabilities, insurers (including the Issuer) invest in a variety of assets that
typically include a large portfolio of fixed income securities. Interest rate volatility can adversely affect



                                                     - 15 -

insurance businesses by reducing the returns earned on, and by reducing the market value of, such
portfolios. Interest rates are sensitive to many factors, including governmental, monetary and tax
policies, domestic and international economic and political considerations, inflation, governmental
debt, the regulatory environment and other factors that are beyond the Issuer's control.

In particular, the Issuer, as with the wider insurance sector, can be adversely impacted by sustained low
interest rates. In times of low interest rates – as experienced between 2008 and 2022 – investment yields
typically decrease. Consequently, when securities in the insurer's existing portfolio mature, the sums
realised are reinvested in securities with lower yields, which in turn decreases the investment income
of the insurer. A protracted period of low interest rates has a negative impact, especially on life insurers
with substantial interest rate guarantees on a traditional book of business where the portfolio yield
approximates the guaranteed interest rate on the policies written. Persistently low interest rates not only
render delivering the necessary return for clients or offering competitive profit sharing more difficult
but also hamper efforts to maintain profitability. Low interest rates also make it difficult to continue to
offer clients attractive life insurance and pension products, which may lead to a reduction in new
business and hence have a negative impact on the Issuer's results of operations. Additionally, if interest
rates decrease, life insurance reserve liabilities (particularly long-tail liabilities) may experience
significant fair value increases, potentially leading to negative solvency impacts (i.e. in case of a
positive interest rate gap).

Conversely, in an environment of rising interest rates, the value of fixed income investments held by
the Issuer may decline, leading to lower unrealised gains or higher unrealised losses. This scenario
could put pressure on the Issuer's investment results, affecting its ability to generate adequate returns
on its investment portfolio.

Moreover, in periods of rising interest rates, there is a heightened risk of policy lapses within the Issuer's
insurance policies. Policyholders may be inclined to seek higher returns available in the market, leading
to increased surrender rates. This trend could result in liquidity challenges for the Issuer, as it would
need to fulfil cash payment obligations to policyholders seeking to withdraw funds. To meet these
obligations, the Issuer may be compelled to sell its investment assets at discounted prices, thereby
incurring investment losses.

The environment of increasing interest rates and increased volatility in interest rates seen in recent years
underscores the relevance of this risk. There is also uncertainty regarding the future direction of rates,
as central banks may adjust monetary policy in response to inflation, economic growth, uncertainty and
conflict in the Middle East or other factors.

Both upward and downward movements in interest rates could have material adverse effects on the
Issuer's premiums, investment income, and overall financial outlook. To reduce the interest rate
sensitivity of its business, the Issuer attempts to match its liabilities with assets whose sensitivity to
interest rates is similar to that of the liabilities, thereby compensating the interest rate risk. However, to
the extent that such asset liability matching is not practicable or fully achieved, fluctuations in the value
of assets and liabilities as interest rates change may have a negative effect on the Issuer's financial
condition and results of operations.

The Issuer is vulnerable to credit spread risk with respect to its fixed income portfolio.

Like most insurance companies, the Issuer has a significant fixed income portfolio in which assets are
typically matched against its insurance liabilities. Its exposure to credit spreads primarily relates to
market price and cash flow variability associated with changes in credit spreads. A spread widening
will reduce the value of fixed income securities held and, conversely, spread tightening will generally
increase the value of fixed income securities in the portfolio. A number of factors can cause an
individual asset or a whole class of assets to decrease in market value, including a perception or fear in
the market that there is an increase in the likelihood of defaults.

it might issue in the financial markets from time to time.

nonetheless generally remain above pre-2022 levels, including across Europe. This environment has

uncertainty and conflict in the Middle East, the long-term inflationary effects of which remain to be

Between 2010 and 2018, the Hellenic Republic experienced substantial strain on its public finances,
prompting it to receive financial assistance through three consecutive support programmes backed by
the European Commission, the European Central Bank ("ECB"), the European Stability Mechanism
("ESM"), and the International Monetary Fund ("IMF"). This period was marked by serious fiscal
challenges and underlying structural weaknesses in the Greek economy. Greece concluded its final
three-year ESM financial assistance programme – known as the "Third Economic Adjustment
Programme" ("EAP") – in August 2018, after which it transitioned into an enhanced surveillance
regime. This framework remained in place until its expiration on 20 August 2022. According to the
European Commission, Greece successfully fulfilled the majority of the policy commitments it had
made to the Eurogroup at the time of its exit from the EAP in June 2018. Since then, oversight of
Greece's economic, fiscal, and financial position has continued through post-programme surveillance
mechanisms and the European Semester process, both integral components of the EU's broader
economic governance framework.

The macroeconomic landscape for Greece remains sensitive to external shocks, particularly geopolitical
tensions and energy price fluctuations affecting travel demand and broader economic conditions. The
Greek economy continued to grow in 2025, outperforming the euro area average for a fifth year in a
row. Real GDP increased by 2.1 per cent. in 2025 year on year (unchanged from 2024). Inflation in the
Greek economy was more or less unchanged in 2025 year on year, with a significant slowdown in the
disinflation seen during the 2023-24 period, mostly on account of persistent services inflation. The
Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices ("HICP") headline inflation rate fell marginally to 2.9 per cent.
(from 3 per cent. in 2024) and remained almost 1 per cent. higher than the respective euro area average
(2.1 per cent.) (Source: Governor's Annual Report, Bank of Greece).

on the Life side of the business (including unit-linked products and health insurance) and €115 million
in Non-Life insurance (including motor, property and other non-life segments). This product diversity
exposes the Issuer to a broader range of insurance liability risks across multiple lines of business than
other insurers in Greece (which are generally limited to offering either life or non-life product lines
only).

Experience in the Issuer's Life and Health businesses could be inconsistent with the assumptions the
Issuer uses to price its products, which could adversely affect its results of operations.

The results of the Issuer's Life and Health businesses depend significantly upon the extent to which its
actual claims experience remains consistent with the assumptions used in the pricing of its products.
Life and Health insurance premiums and long-term liabilities are calculated using assumptions as to
mortality, disability, interest rates, and expenses used to project future liabilities. Although experience
(i.e. the claims and expenses as actually incurred) is closely monitored, there is no guarantee that actual
experience will match the assumptions that were used in initially establishing future policyholder
benefits and related premium levels.

The actuarial assumptions underlying technical provisions, including mortality, morbidity, lapse and
surrender behaviour, expenses, claims frequency, severity and inflation are inherently volatile, as they
reflect future events that can only be projected based on historical experience and forward-looking
judgement. Their values are sensitive to demographic shifts, medical and technological developments,
policyholder behaviour and trends, market conditions, regulatory changes and macroeconomic factors
such as interest rates and market performance, all of which can move materially over relatively short
horizons. Therefore, even small movements in key assumptions can produce significant changes in the
financial statements of an insurance entity. Recognising this volatility, the actuarial function performs
regular experience analyses, sensitivity and stress tests, and assumption reviews, ensuring that technical
provisions remain a faithful and prudent reflection of the ultimate cost of the Issuer's obligations to
policyholders. However, there is no guarantee that these adjustments will be wholly successful or
sufficient in mitigating against these movements in key assumptions and the consequent impact on the
results of operations of the Issuer's Life and Health businesses. Regulatory constraints may also affect
the ability of the Issuer adequately to adjust the price of relevant insurance products, particularly as
regards long-term health insurance contracts.

Furthermore, among the Life products marketed or historically sold by the Issuer, a subset of these
products is related to contracts with guaranteed investment returns. Interest rates in Europe have
experienced notable changes, with recent movements reflecting a shift from the previously sustained
lower levels. Since interest rates remain volatile or could increase further, and despite discontinuation
of underwriting of certain products with high guaranteed rates, the Issuer could potentially be required
to provide additional funds to its Life business to support its obligations in respect of products with
higher guaranteed returns, which could in turn have a material adverse effect on the Issuer's financial
condition and results of operations.

The Issuer is subject to risks concerning the adequacy of its technical provisions.

The technical provisions of the Issuer are designed to cover the present value of its net future obligations
towards policyholders, together with a risk margin (in accordance with Solvency II) and, where
applicable, a contractual service margin ("CSM") and risk adjustment (under IFRS 17). They are
calculated in respect of the Issuer's Life and Health businesses and include, inter alia, mathematical
provisions, provisions for reported and unreported claims and unearned premium provisions under the
statutory/Solvency II framework, as well as the liability for incurred claims (reported and unreported)
and the liability for remaining coverage under IFRS 17. These technical provisions, together with the
assets backing them, represent a major part of the Issuer's balance sheet. Their adequacy depends on
actual future outcomes, in particular the level, timing, and cost of claims, and should those outcomes
deviate adversely from the assumptions underlying the calculation of the related provisions, such
provisions, as currently recognised, may prove to be insufficient.

The Issuer's results of operations depend significantly on the extent to which its actual claims experience
is consistent with the assumptions used in pricing its products and in establishing its technical provisions
and claims liabilities. Reserve estimates are reviewed and adjusted periodically based on the most
current information available to management, with any resulting changes recognised either in the
current period results of operations or, under IFRS 17, through an adjustment to the CSM for changes
relating to future service. Where, for a group of insurance contracts, unfavourable changes in the
fulfilment cash flows relating to future service exceed the carrying amount of the CSM, IFRS 17
requires the recognition of a loss component, with the excess charged immediately to the Issuer's profit
and loss account.

Although the Issuer maintains actuarial methodologies, experience monitoring processes and a
reserving governance framework designed to identify and manage reserve risk on a timely basis, there
can be no assurance that its technical provisions will prove sufficient to cover its ultimate insurance
losses, expenses, or future policyholder benefits. Should they prove inadequate, the Issuer would be
required to strengthen its technical provisions, resulting in a charge to earnings and a reduction in own
funds, which could adversely affect its results of operations, solvency position, and financial condition.

The Issuer's Non-Life business is subject to insurance underwriting risks.

Underwriting risk can be generally defined as a change in the value of insurance liabilities which is
caused by the final costs for full contractual obligations varying from those assumed when these
obligations were estimated. Non-Life insurance underwriting risks are divided into premium risk,
catastrophe risk and reserve risk.

Premium risk relates to future claims resulting from expected insured events which have not occurred
by the balance sheet date. The frequency, severity and timing of insured events, and hence future claims,
may differ from those expected. As a result, the claims cost for future claims exceeds the expected level
resulting in a loss or adverse changes in the value of insurance liabilities.

Catastrophe risk can be seen as an extreme case of premium risk. It is the risk of extreme or exceptional
events, such as natural disasters (for example, windstorms, floods, cloudbursts, snowstorms, fires and
hail) or man-made catastrophes such as acts of terrorism, where the pricing and setting of provisioning
assumptions include significant uncertainty. These events may lead to significant deviations between
actual claims and the total expected claims, resulting in a loss or adverse changes in the value of
insurance liabilities.

Reserve risk relates to incurred claims resulting from insured events which have occurred at or prior to
the balance sheet date. The final amount, frequency and timing of claims payments may differ from
those originally expected. In particular, cost inflation assumptions are important in the underwriting
process. The extent of cost inflation risk is largely dependent on the type of product and business. For



                                                   - 25 -

example, the Health business is exposed to medical and healthcare costs as well as legislative changes
in respect of injury compensation. Other reserve risks also stem from uncertainty in the claim amounts
caused by higher-than-expected claims inflation, increased retirement age and increased life
expectancy. Should the Issuer's estimation of cost inflation be inadequate, the premium indexation may
be too low. As a result, technical provisions will not be sufficient to cover the cost for already incurred
claims and there will be a loss or adverse change in the value of insurance liabilities.

Realisation of risks that are larger than anticipated at the time of pricing is possible and may have a
material adverse effect on the Issuer's business, operations and financial condition.

Financial results may be affected by insurance claims.

Insurance claims are the Issuer's principal expense, and it could take several years before all claims that
have occurred during any given accounting period are reported and settled. Accordingly, the frequency
and severity of incurred and reported insurance claims are an important part of the Issuer's overall
profitability, and fluctuations in insurance claims can have a material effect on its results of operations.
Furthermore, the diversity of the Issuer's insurance risks makes it more difficult to identify individual
judgments and assumptions that are more likely than others to have a material impact on the future
development of its insurance liabilities. For example, the estimation of provisions for the ultimate costs
of liability-, personal accident- and illness-related claims is subject to a range of uncertainties that are
generally greater than those encountered for other classes of business (such as motor or property), due
to the slow emergence and longer settlement period for these claims. In addition, any unexpected
adverse changes in the rate of claims inflation, cost inflation or in the cost and availability of reinsurance
protection may have a material adverse effect on the Issuer's financial position, solvency, results of
operations and cash flows. Changes in these factors can be very difficult to predict, and recent years
have been characterised by dramatic weather conditions leading to a significant number of insurance
claims.

The Issuer is exposed to longevity risk in its annuity portfolio.

Uncertainty in the future development of longevity is inherent to a long-term life insurance business
and cannot be fully eliminated. A strengthening of the longevity assumption (that is, an assumption that
policyholders, on average, live longer than previously expected) may be required to reflect either
changes in the life expectancy of the general population (for example, as a result of healthier lifestyles,
or the increased availability and effectiveness of medical treatments) or changes specific to the
experience of the Issuer's own portfolio used to value its long-term business liabilities. Any such
strengthening would lead to an increase in technical provisions and, under IFRS 17, to a corresponding
reduction in the CSM.

Any decrease in the amount of the Issuer's reinsurance cover relative to its primary insurance liability

reinsurers to meet their financial obligations to the Issuer could materially adversely affect the Issuer's

The Issuer is subject to emerging insurance risks.

The insurance business and market is subject to emerging risks. By their very nature these risks are

The EU has developed a solvency framework for insurance and reinsurance companies operating in the

Directive entered into force on 1 January 2016. While a number of changes have since been
implemented, further changes remain to be implemented.

The Solvency II approach to solvency is based on the concept of three pillars:

•       Pillar 1 – eligible funds and capital requirements;

•       Pillar 2 – supervisory review of the company's assessment of risk; and

•       Pillar 3 – enhanced disclosure requirements.

A key aspect of Solvency II is that capital requirements are assessed on a risk-based approach.

On 10 October 2014, the European Commission adopted the Solvency II Regulation supplementing
Directive 2009/138/EC on valuation and risk-based capital requirements (pillar I), enhanced governance
(pillar II) and increased transparency (pillar III).

Since the implementation of the Solvency II regime, further changes to the rules have been introduced,

issued two sets of advice to the European Commission on specific items in the Solvency II Regulation.

undertakings requiring public financial support, and (ii) the commencement of resolution procedures
when insurance or reinsurance undertakings are failing or likely to fail, where there is no prospect that
private sector alternatives or supervisory measures would prevent such failure. In the event of
resolution, the IRRD grants resolution authorities the power to apply a range of resolution tools,
including the write-down and conversion tool, which allow resolution authorities to write down, or
convert to equity, capital instruments, debt instruments and other eligible liabilities of insurance
undertakings, generally corresponding to their ranking in liquidation, such that share capital would be
expected to suffer the first losses (via its cancellation or transfer to creditors whose claims have been
converted), then other tier 1 instruments (such as the Notes), then tier 2 instruments and then other
instruments with a higher ranking in liquidation. Upon the adoption of the resolution tools, including
the write-down and conversion tool, holders of Notes could be exposed to significant risks, potentially
losing all or part (which could be substantially all) of their investment in the Notes if the Issuer was to
experience financial difficulties and be deemed to be failing or likely to fail. In addition, if the Issuer's

powers could cause the market value and/or the liquidity of the Notes to decline more rapidly and/or to

Factors – Risks relating to the Notes – The Issuer, any member of an applicable Solvency II Group

On 28 January 2025, the IRRD entered into force. EU Member States are required to adopt
implementing legislation by 29 January 2027. As at the date of this Offering Circular, implementation
of the IRRD in Greece is still pending. However, certain resolution powers already apply to insurance
undertakings in Greece under Greek Law 4364/2016, including: (i) the suspension of the payment of

measures for an anticipated winding-up adopted by an insurance administrator.

The IRRD requires EU Member States to implement preventative measures to reduce the likelihood of
insurance undertakings requiring public financial support and to equip resolution authorities with
resolution tools to be used when in-scope undertakings are failing or are likely to fail, with no reasonable
prospect of other actions preventing such failure within a reasonable time. A key resolution tool within
the IRRD is the power to write down or convert capital instruments and eligible liabilities, on which
basis the competent resolution authority may write down or (with the exception of shares) convert
capital instruments, debt instruments and other eligible liabilities of insurance undertakings into shares,
generally in inverse order of their ranking in liquidation, in accordance with the applicable creditor
hierarchy. The tool would apply first to share capital (via its cancellation or transfer to creditors whose
claims have been converted), then to tier 1 instruments (such as the Notes) other than shares, then to
tier 2 instruments, then to tier 3 instruments and then to other instruments with a higher ranking in
liquidation, if the undertaking is failing or likely to fail and certain other conditions are met or if the
conditions for group resolution are met. Save for some limited exceptions, all insurance and other
liabilities will be eligible for write-down.

Following the First Reset Date, interest amounts payable under the Notes are calculated from time to

This swap-rate, the Euro Interbank Offered Rate ("EURIBOR") underlying the floating leg of this swap
rate and other interest rates or other types of rates and indices which are deemed "benchmarks" (each a
"Benchmark") have, in recent years, been the subject of political and regulatory scrutiny as to how
they are created and operated. This has resulted in regulatory reform and changes to existing
Benchmarks, including, in June 2016, pursuant to the entry into force of Regulation (EU) 2016/1011
on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts or to measure the
performance of investment funds. These reforms may cause a Benchmark to perform differently than
in the past, or to disappear entirely, or to have other consequences which cannot be predicted. Any such
consequence could have a material adverse effect on the Notes.

Under the Conditions, certain benchmark replacement provisions will apply if a Benchmark (or any
component part thereof) used as a reference for the calculation of interest amounts payable under the
Notes were to be discontinued or otherwise became unavailable.

If a Benchmark Event occurs, the Issuer shall use its reasonable endeavours to appoint an Independent
Adviser, which must be an independent financial institution of international repute or other independent
adviser experienced in the international debt capital markets. Such Independent Adviser will be tasked
with determining whether an officially recognised Successor Reference Rate to the discontinued
Benchmark exists. If that is not the case, the Independent Adviser will attempt to find an Alternative
Reference Rate. If the Independent Adviser determines a Successor Reference Rate or Alternative
Reference Rate, such Successor Reference Rate or Alternative Reference Rate will replace the previous
Benchmark for purposes of determining the relevant Interest Rate and the Independent Adviser shall
apply an Adjustment Spread to such Successor Reference Rate or Alternative Reference Rate. Such
determination will (in the absence of manifest error) be binding for the Issuer, the Agent, Paying Agent
and the Noteholders. In addition, if amendments to the Conditions are required to ensure the proper
operation of the Successor Reference Rate, the Alternative Reference Rate or the Adjustment Spread,
the Issuer shall vary the Conditions accordingly, without any requirement for the consent or approval
of the Noteholders.

RISKS RELATING TO THE MARKET GENERALLY

The secondary market generally.

The Notes will have no established trading market when issued, and one may never develop including
(without limitation) as a result of the Notes being purchased initially by a single investor or a limited
number of initial investors. If a market for the Notes does develop it may not be liquid. Investors may
not be able to sell their Notes easily or at prices that will provide them with a yield comparable to similar
investments that have a developed secondary market and/or which are rated. This will particularly be
the case if the Notes are issued to a single investor or a limited number of initial investors. Illiquidity
may have a severely adverse effect on the market value of the Notes.

If the Issuer's financial condition deteriorates such that there is an increased risk that the Issuer may be
wound-up or liquidated, or if at any time there is any actual or anticipated cancellation of interest or
deferral of redemption and/or any risk of early redemption in accordance with the Conditions, such
circumstances can be expected to have a material adverse effect on the market price of the Notes.
Investors in the Notes may find it difficult to sell their Notes in such circumstances, or may only be able
to sell their Notes at a price which may be significantly lower than the price at which they purchased
their Notes. In such a sale, investors may lose some or substantially all of their investment in the Notes.

Exchange rate risks and exchange controls.

The Issuer will pay principal and interest on Notes in euro. This presents certain risks relating to
currency conversions if an investor's financial activities are denominated principally in a currency or
currency unit (the "Investor's Currency") other than euro. These include the risk that exchange rates
may significantly change (including changes due to devaluation of euro or revaluation of the Investor's
Currency) and the risk that authorities with jurisdiction over the Investor's Currency may impose or
modify exchange controls. An appreciation in the value of the Investor's Currency relative to euro would
decrease (1) the Investor's Currency-equivalent yield on the Notes, (2) the Investor's Currency-
equivalent value of the principal payable on the Notes and (3) the Investor's Currency-equivalent market
value of the Notes.

Government and monetary authorities may impose (as some have done in the past) exchange controls
that could adversely affect an applicable exchange rate. As a result, investors may receive less interest
or principal than expected, or no interest or principal.

Interest rate risks.

Investment in the Notes, which bear a fixed rate of interest which is reset on each Reset Date, involves
the risk that subsequent increases in market interest rates may adversely affect the market value of the
Notes.

Since the Notes are held by or on behalf of Euroclear and Clearstream, Luxembourg, investors will
have to rely on the clearing system procedures for transfer, payment and communication with the
Issuer.

The Notes will, upon issue, be represented by a Global Certificate that will be deposited with, and
registered in the name of a nominee for, a common depositary for Euroclear and Clearstream,
Luxembourg. Euroclear and Clearstream, Luxembourg will maintain records of the beneficial interests
in the Global Certificate. While the Notes are in global form, investors will be able to trade their
beneficial interests only through Euroclear or Clearstream, Luxembourg, as the case may be.

While the Notes are in global form, the payment obligations of the Issuer under the Notes will be
discharged upon such payments being made by or on behalf of the Issuer to or to the order of the
nominee for the common depositary. A holder of a beneficial interest in a Note must rely on the
procedures of Euroclear and/or Clearstream, Luxembourg, as the case may be, to receive payments
under the Notes. The Issuer does not have any responsibility or liability for the records relating to, or
payments made in respect of, beneficial interests in the Global Certificate.

Accordingly, it is possible that the Notes may be traded in the clearing systems in amounts in excess of

will be issued in principal amounts of €200,000 and higher integral multiples of €1,000 but will in no

may not receive a Certificate (should Certificates be printed) in respect of such holding. Such a
Noteholder would need to purchase a principal amount of Notes such that its holding amounts to
€200,000 in order to receive a Certificate.

that is not an integral multiple of €200,000 may be illiquid and difficult to trade.

DESCRIPTION OF THE ISSUER

Overview

The Issuer, whose trading name is Ethniki Asfalistiki, is the first and oldest insurance company in
Greece, established 135 years ago on 15 June 1891. The Issuer is headquartered at 103-105 Syngrou
Avenue, GR-117 45 Athens, Greece, its telephone number is +30 210 9099000 and its website is
https://www.ethnikiasfalistiki.gr/en.

Pursuant to its articles of association, the Issuer's purpose is to carry out insurance, reinsurance and
related financial activities for insurance companies under applicable Greek and EU law, including
Greek Law 4548/2018 and Greek Law 4364/2016.

History of the Issuer

The Issuer was established in 1891 and has developed a strong reputation by consistently delivering on
its commitments to the environment, people and communities, while maintaining a human-centred
orientation and seeking to provide relevant and high-quality services to its customers.

In the context of its 135-year history, the Issuer has served millions of customers and has continued to
evolve its products, services and capabilities to meet changing customer needs and expectations. The
Issuer's ambition is to continue to contribute positively to the Greek economy and society while creating
enduring value for customers, partners and employees.

In November 2025, Piraeus Financial Holdings S.A. concluded the acquisition of 100 per cent. of the
shares of Ethniki Holdings S.à r.l. ("Ethniki Holdings"), the parent company of the Issuer, from CVC
Capital Partners Fund VII and National Bank of Greece, thereby becoming the sole shareholder of the
Issuer through Ethniki Holdings. This transaction marked a new chapter for the Issuer and created
significant opportunities for growth and value creation. In December 2025, Piraeus Bank S.A.
("Piraeus") concluded a reverse merger and absorption of Piraeus Financial Holdings S.A. and,
accordingly, Piraeus became the ultimate parent company of the Issuer.

In 2025, the Issuer sharpened its strategic focus on the Greek market, completing the divestment of its
operations in Cyprus and Romania, which has optimised capital allocation and reduced organisational
complexity.

In September 2025, the Issuer completed the acquisition of a 55 per cent. majority stake in Elysee
Insurance Agent & Coordinator S.A. and Elysee Insurance Brokers S.A., which are leading insurance
distribution companies active across all insurance lines in Greece. The transaction was intended to
expand the Issuer's product distribution channels, create new growth opportunities and diversify its
sources of revenue.

The Issuer's 2025 results reflected the completion of a strategic transformation cycle and the transition
to a more modern, efficient and agile operating model. The integration into the Piraeus group is intended
to provide stability, growth prospects and meaningful value creation for stakeholders.

Organisational structure

The Issuer is wholly owned by Ethniki Holdings. As at 31 December 2025, the Issuer had share capital
of €235,220,976 divided into 196,017,480 registered voting shares with a nominal value of €1.20 each.

The only material assets of Ethniki Holdings are its shareholdings in the Issuer and it does not carry out
any trading activity on its own account.

As at the date of this Offering Circular, the Issuer is the parent undertaking of two subsidiaries, Elysee
Insurance Agent & Coordinator S.A. and Elysee Insurance Brokers S.A., and a subsidiary undertaking
of its ultimate parent company, Piraeus.

Mission and strategy

The Issuer's stated mission is to support people and businesses by offering simple, innovative and
reliable solutions to protect what matters most to them. Its stated vision is to be the leading insurer in
Greece, standing by its customers and redefining insurance with empathy and simplicity while building
a sustainable future. Its values are integrity and reliability, customer centricity, simplicity and
efficiency, performance and excellence, innovation, and ownership and accountability.

The Issuer's strategy focuses on accelerating growth, enhancing profitability and managing capital
efficiently, with the objective of creating sustainable value for its customers, partners and shareholders.
Its strategic priorities include strengthening and expanding its commercial network, further developing
the health and property and casualty business lines, enhancing operational efficiency through
disciplined underwriting and claims management, strengthening the balance sheet, focusing on
customer experience, developing people and culture, and leveraging technology and data to support
transformation.

For the 2026-2030 period, the Issuer's business strategy will focus on sustainable value creation through
a balanced approach to growth, profitability and resilience. This strategy is supported by a strong capital
base and high liquidity, which are key factors enabling disciplined growth and the absorption of
volatility. Prudent investment and risk management support strategic flexibility and provide a
foundation for sustainable profitability.

The Issuer is focused on the Greek insurance market, which continues to be characterised by significant
growth potential, driven by low insurance penetration and a substantial protection gap. The Issuer's
integration into the Piraeus group ecosystem creates opportunities to accelerate growth through
synergies, expanded distribution channels and a stronger customer base.

The Issuer seeks to maintain a diversified model across products and distribution channels. It offers
insurance products and services through a multi-channel approach comprising exclusive and non-
exclusive agents, independent brokers, bancassurance and direct channels.

As part of its growth strategy, the Issuer has taken steps to diversify revenue streams and expand
distribution. The acquisition of a majority stake in the Elysee insurance brokerage companies is
intended to strengthen its position in the motor line of business, diversifying revenue streams and
establishing foundations for a broader mobility ecosystem.

sustainable value for customers, partners and its shareholder.

APM Definitions

"Adjusted operating profit before tax": a measure of underlying operating profitability, determined
as profit before tax, adjusted for the effect of non-operating / non-recurring and other notable items.

"Non-operating / non-recurring items" may include the following:

(i)      one-time effects from significant transactions with disposal character (such as the gain or loss
         on the disposal of a subsidiary or a real estate property);

(ii)     voluntary exit scheme related expenses;

(iii)    interest expense from external debt;

(iv)     realised and unrealised gains/losses from financial assets measured at fair value excluding unit-
         linked assets;

(v)      restructuring, integration and transaction related expenses, that are considered non-recurring
         items based on management judgement; and

(vi)     litigation and other expenses / income with a one-off character.

"Other notable items" reflect the unexpected impact of events that affect the Issuer's results, which may
include the revision of non-economic assumptions and any prior-year reserves developments (positive
or negative) primarily related to non-life and health businesses.




                                                   - 122 -

"Investment portfolio return": an investment performance metric that indicates how effectively a
portfolio of assets generates income relative to its book value during the period the amount invested. It
is calculated as investment income divided by the average investment portfolio.

"Investment income" is the net investment income from financial assets as derived from financial
statements, excluding the investment income generated from unit-linked financial assets, loans,
investment property assets and interest expense from subordinated loans and investment contracts.

"Investment portfolio" is the value of total financial assets, as derived from financial statements,
including cash and cash equivalents but excluding unit-linked financial assets and loans.

"Average investment portfolio" is determined as the average between the investment portfolio at the
start of the period and at the end of the period.

"Return on capital employed": a financial performance metric that measures how efficiently a
company is using its capital to generate profits. It is calculated as adjusted operating profit before
interest and tax divided by average capital employed.

"Adjusted operating profit before interest and tax" is adjusted operating profit before tax (as described
above).

"Capital employed" is the sum of shareholders' equity plus the external debt outstanding nominal
balances.

"Average capital employed" is determined as the average between the capital employed at the start of
the period and at the end of the period.

"Return on equity": a financial performance metric that measures how efficiently a company is using
its shareholders' equity to generate profits. It is calculated as adjusted operating profit after tax divided
by average shareholders' equity.

"Adjusted operating profit after tax" is the adjusted operating profit before tax (as described above) plus
interest expense from external debt and related income tax expense.

"Shareholders' equity" is the total of share capital, reserves, and retained earnings (or accumulated
losses) of the company, as reflected on the statement of financial position.

"Average shareholders' equity" is determined as the average between shareholders' equity at the start
of the period and at the end of the period.

"Stock of future profit": represents future profit recognised in the Issuer's statement of financial
position that will be released in the income statement over time. It is calculated as the sum of the
contractual service margin and risk adjustment (excluding risk adjustment of liability of incurred
claims), as derived from the financial statements.

"Combined ratio": a financial measure of whether an insurer is making an underwriting profit from its
core insurance activities, before considering investment income. It is mainly used for measuring
underwriting profitability for short-term products (i.e. Non-Life, Health and Protection related
insurance contracts). It is calculated as the sum of loss ratio and the expense ratio.

"Loss ratio" indicates the underwriting performance of an insurer, including whether premiums are
appropriately priced relative to the risks insured. It is calculated as claims and benefits, net of
reinsurance and less reinsurance commissions contingent on claims, divided by insurance revenue, net
of reinsurance and including ordinary commissions from reinsurers.



                                                   - 123 -

"Expense ratio" is calculated as operating expenses plus gross commission expense, divided by
insurance revenue net of reinsurance and including ordinary commissions from reinsurers.

"Expense rate": measures operating efficiency by comparing total expenses, with total gross written
premiums for the period.
